items.title: 'Transporter' held with RM739,200 worth of smuggled cigarettes
items.summary: The suspect received RM5,000 a month to distribute untaxed cigarettes in the local market. "Initial interrogation found that the suspect claimed to have been involved in transporting cigarettes for about two years and received RM5,000 a month to distribute untaxed cigarettes. "The suspect also claimed that he received instructions from a Bangladeshi man to distribute the cigarettes," he said.

items.title: Three houses in Sungai Petani village hit by mudslide
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: Three houses in Kampung Serukam here were affected by a mudslide following heavy rain this afternoon. The incident is believed to have occurred after heavy rain began at 12.30 pm, causing a collapse at a nearby housing project site, before water and mud flowed into residents' homes. Meanwhile, Scientex SP Astana project site supervisor Mohd Haniff Ramli said three houses were affected in the incident, including two located within the project site.

items.title: Hulu Selangor roads to close in stages for LTdL stage 5 on Oct 1
items.summary: Hulu Selangor police chief superintendent M Manimaran said the road closures would involve routes from KM79 of Jalan Kuala Lumpur-Ipoh at the Muallim district border, Ulu Bernam-Kalumpang-Kerling-Kuala Kubu Baru-Pekan Batang Kali to the Gohtong Jaya Roundabout. "As such, road users are advised to use alternative routes, namely Serendah-Sungai Choh-Bukit Beruntung-Bukit Beruntung Toll-North-South Expressway-Tanjung Malim Toll; Batang Kali-Hulu Yam Bharu-Pekan Hulu Yam-Hulu Yam Lama-Serendah; and Batang Kali-Hulu Yam Bharu-Sungai Tua-Middle Ring Road 2-Gombak Toll-Genting Highlands," he said in a statement. Manimaran said the road closures are expected to end at 1 pm, depending on the movement and routes taken by the riders.

items.title: MACC proposes governance improvements for Felda, two subsidiaries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has proposed governance improvements to the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and two of its subsidiaries to strengthen the management of two projects under the agency. In a statement, MACC said the subsidiaries involved were FIC Supplies Sdn Bhd (FIC Supplies) and FIC Integrated Property Management (FIC IPM). The recommendations were put forward by MACC's Governance Investigation Division (BPT) to enhance governance in the implementation of the Agro Park (Commercial) Project and the Cattle Trading Pilot Project.

items.title: US-led coalition ends mission in Iraq
items.summary: BAGHDAD: A US-led coalition deployed in Iraq more than a decade ago to fight jihadists concluded its mission on Wednesday, a move celebrated by the country's leaders, but which some fear will embolden pro-Iran armed factions. Coalition troops deployed to Iraq and Syria in 2014 to fight the Islamic State group, which had seized large swathes of territory, committing massacres and forcing thousands of women and children into slavery. The group was defeated in Iraq in 2017 and in Syria in 2019, but coalition forces stayed on to battle the group's remnants.

items.title: SpaceX contributes 50 starlink kits to support Malaysia's disaster preparedness
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: United States Aerospace Company, SpaceX, donated 50 units of Starlink kits to Malaysia to support the country's disaster preparedness, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said the contribution was presented by a SpaceX delegation during a courtesy call at the Perdana Putra Building in Putrajaya, which was also attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Anwar said the meeting, among other things, discussed efforts to strengthen strategic cooperation through Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by the company, with a specific focus on expanding network access to residents in rural areas.

items.title: Firefighters wade through floodwaters for 2km to rescue seven in Klang
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Firefighters waded through waist-deep floodwaters for two kilometres to rescue a family of seven, including four children, who were trapped by flash floods at Taman Rashna, Klang. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said firefighters had to make the journey on foot as the high water level prevented their fire engine from reaching the affected residential area. [[nid:1544896]] "Firefighters had to walk two kilometres to reach the affected residential area.

items.title: Passenger on rerouted flydubai flight says pilot tried to crash plane
items.summary: TABUK, Saudi Arabia: A passenger on a rerouted flydubai flight that was bound for Tel Aviv said one of the pilots tried to crash the plane and kill everyone on board, after both pilots were found to be wounded on landing in Saudi Arabia. The flydubai plane was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk "at 9.45am (0645 GMT) and its captain and copilot were found to have injuries and were transported to hospital", a statement from the company operating the airport said. The low-cost carrier had earlier said flight FZ 1073 "experienced an incident while en route.

items.title: #NSTviral: Motorcyclist wins hearts clearing drain in Johor Baru floods [WATCH]
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A motorcyclist braved fast-rising floodwaters to clear a blocked drain beneath the Taman Perling flyover in Johor Baru. The man was seen walking through floodwater along Jalan Skudai beneath the flyover after heavy rain caused flash floods in several parts of the city. Several netizens praised the man, saying his actions helped clear the obstruction and allowed the stagnant floodwater to drain more quickly.

items.title: Housewife's RM6,000 'Immigration officer' act busted
items.summary: AYER KEROH: A housewife in her 50s allegedly charged RM6,000 per client by posing as a senior immigration department officer and offering to arrange work permits for foreigners. Melaka Immigration director Anirwan Fauzee Mohd Aini said the woman was arrested following a complaint and intelligence gathering by the department's enforcement division. "The suspect is believed to have posed as a senior immigration director at the headquarters and the immigration department's integrity chief.

items.title: Zetrix, IPVG extend RM130mil MyEG Ventures deal deadline
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd and IPVG Employees Inc have extended the deadline by three months to complete the former's acquisition of a 50 per cent stake in Philippines-based MyEG Ventures Inc. Zetrix AI said both parties agreed to complete the share purchase agreement by the end of the fourth quarter, instead of the original deadline of Wednesday. Zetrix AI said the extension mainly allows more time to fulfil the conditions precedent under the agreement. On Sept 1, Zetrix AI agreed to buy the 50 per cent stake from Next Lion Ltd, whose sole shareholder and director is Yap Shon Leong.

items.title: MLFF implementation not to be rushed – Nanta
items.summary: He said the parties involved had been given a timeline to work out the details, with several platforms already being considered, although negotiations were still ongoing. Nanta said the implementation would follow a business-to-business (B2B) model, with highway concessionaires and other interested parties working together to develop the system. Nanta said the approach would allow interested parties to negotiate among themselves, particularly highway concessionaires, which own the highways and related assets.

items.title: Batu Kawan clears 95pct in MKH takeover
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Kawan Bhd's unconditional mandatory takeover of MKH Bhd has crossed the 95 per cent threshold, paving the way for the property developer to be delisted from Bursa Malaysia. As at market close on Wednesday, Batu Kawan and its wholly owned unit Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd, together with parties acting in concert, held 548.85 million MKH shares. Bursa Malaysia will suspend trading in MKH shares five market days from Oct 8.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines -September 30, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Nepal expedites confirmation Nepal has agreed to expedite confirmation of the status of 55 Malaysians still untraced following the disaster. Hostel student beaten A Form Two student who died after alleged bullying at a Kuala Pilah hostel was beaten with a rubber hose before being found unconscious. Myanmar detainees repatriated A total of 3,542 Myanmar detainees will be repatriated in the second phase, following the return of 1,476 yesterday.

items.title: RM100mil spent on JB flood mitigation, but system overwhelmed by intense rain
items.summary: He said the combination placed significant pressure on the city's drainage and flood mitigation systems. Jafni said rainfall between 1pm and 7pm totalled about 90mm, with rainfall increasing significantly between 1.30pm and 5pm. "This can cause a backwater effect, slowing drainage flow and raising water levels upstream," he said.

items.title: Singapore launches dating service for public servants
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore has launched a dating platform for public officials, in the city-state's latest experiment meant to tackle declining marriage and historically low fertility rates. Public officials can fill out details including interests, habits, religious preferences and "dealbreakers." Singapore, which has a population of just over six million people, saw record-low fertility rates last year.

items.title: Rejoining EU among options for future ties - UK PM
items.summary: LONDON: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in an interview broadcast Wednesday that rejoining the EU was among the potential answers to the unavoidable question of what Britain's future relationship with Europe could look like. Britain voted to leave the bloc in the contentious 2016 Brexit referendum. Burnham, who campaigned to stay in the EU, has previously said he hoped Britain would return to the 27-nation bloc within his lifetime.

items.title: Five charged over alleged false documents in hardcore poor house repairs
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A civil servant and four company owners were charged in the Special Corruption Court here today over alleged offences involving repair works on houses under the Hardcore Poor Housing Programme (PPRT). Aidah faces 10 charges, while Kenidi and Mohd Nur face five charges each. Four of the charges against Aidah involve submitting invoices containing false documents to the then Sabah GiatMara director in relation to repair works on PPRT houses for several recipients.

items.title: Astro slips into RM25.8mil net loss in Q2
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Astro Malaysia Holdings Bhd slipped into a net loss in the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 with a net loss of RM25.80 million, compared with a net profit of RM16.39 million a year ago. Revenue fell 7.2 per cent to RM633.75 million from RM683.21 million, mainly due to lower contributions from its subscription and advertising businesses. Revenue from its television segment fell RM49 million, or 7.5 per cent, to RM606 million from RM655 million in the corresponding quarter, while radio revenue declined marginally by RM0.4 million, or 1.4 per cent.

items.title: In Johor Bahru, firemen rescue 44 pupils and teachers in kindergarten trapped by flash flood
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 – Firemen managed to rescue 37 pupils and seven teachers who were earlier trapped in the Umiku Sayang Kindergarten and Nursery on Jalan Muhd Amin here after it was inundated by a flash floods today. Larkin Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Senior Fire Officer I Nakish Nekmat said that authorities received an distress call regarding the incident at 3.53pm. Following the call, a team of 10 firemen – equipped with a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit – were dispatched to the scene that was located about 10 kilometres away.

items.title: Prisons Department delegation visits Balai Berita
items.summary: The delegation, led by Prisons Policy Division senior director Mohamad Rosidek Musa and comprising six officers, was received by Media Prima News and Current Affairs (NCA) Group Managing Editor Jasbant Singh. Also present were Media Prima NCA Group Deputy Managing Editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim, NCA Television Networks Group Editor Datuk Azhari Muhidin and NCA Convergence Operations Editor-In-Chief M Thillinadan. Also attending were Harian Metro Group Editor Hussin Jahit and NCA Convergence Operations Deputy Editors Yusri Abdul Halim, Datuk Sariha Mohd Ali, and Robin Augustin The visit aimed to strengthen strategic cooperation and enhance media coverage of prison-related and social issues.

items.title: Ex-EPF CEO proposes employers pay higher EPF contributions for low-wage workers while reducing contributions for high-income staff
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — To help lower-salary workers save up more money for their retirement through the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), their employers could help put in more money towards their EPF savings, former EPF CEO Tan Sri Shahril Ridza Ridzuan said today. Shahril, currently Axiata Group Berhad’s chairman, noted that Malaysia currently has one of the highest contribution rates from employees and their employers for retirement savings in EPF. Currently in Malaysia, the law requires Malaysian employees below age 60 to contribute 11 per cent of their salary into their EPF retirement savings, while employers will have to contribute 13 per cent of the salary (if the employee’s salary is below RM5,000) or 12 per cent (if above RM5,000).

items.title: Johari vows to address Titiwangsa residents' concerns
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Titiwangsa member of parliament Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani has pledged to address concerns raised by residents in the constituency, including on the lack of suitable recreational facilities for children. Johari, who is also investment, trade and industry minister, said he was open to meeting joint management bodies (JMBs) and management corporations (MC) in his constituency to discuss issues affecting residents. Akhmal also proposed facilities such as futsal and badminton courts for residents.

items.title: Divfex secures RM120mil data centre equipment supply contracts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Divfex Bhd (DFX) has secured two separate supply agreements worth a combined RM120.12 million for the procurement and supply of key equipments for a 15-megawatt (MW) data centre fit-out in Penang. The company said its wholly owned subsidiary, Diversified Gateway Bhd (DGB), and its 51 per cent-owned subsidiary, Excel Commerce Solutions Sdn Bhd (EXCEL), signed the agreements with a leading Malaysian-incorporated data centre company involved in the provision of data centre facility services and related infrastructure today. Under the first supply agreement, DGB would supply generator sets, transformers, switchgear and low-voltage equipment for RM84.44 million, while EXCEL would supply cables under the second agreement for RM35.67 million.

items.title: Several areas in Johor Bahru hit by flash floods following heavy rain (VIDEO)
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 – Several areas in the Johor Bahru district and city were hit by flash floods following a heavy afternoon downpour. https://www.facebook.com/share/v/19Y6wverdL/?mibextid=wwXIfr The roads affected were Jalan Kolam Air, Jalan Ayer Molek, Jalan Yahya Awal, Jalan Pantai and Jalan Wong Ah Fook in the city. https://www.facebook.com/100093466671276/videos/himpunan-rakaman-video-keadaan-banjir-kilat-di-sekitar-pusat-bandaraya-johor-bah/1939811560728289/

items.title: UWC FY26 net profit jumps to RM93.83mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: UWC Bhd's net profit jumped to RM93.83 million in the financial year ended July 31, 2026 (FY26) from RM40.51 million a year ago. The engineering services company said its revenue also increased to RM594.89 million compared with RM386.17 million previously. For the fourth quarter ended July 31, 2026, UWC recorded a higher net profit of RM37.59 million from RM16.36 million, while revenue rose to RM186.17 million from RM108.79 million previously.

items.title: Anwar hails UM for breaking into world top 200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Universiti Malaya (UM) on becoming the first Malaysian university to break into the top 200 of the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027. He said UM's ranking of 194th in the list reflected the university's excellence in teaching and research. Anwar said the achievement also instilled confidence that local higher education institutions were capable of competing with leading universities worldwide.

items.title: Five remanded after fake gold bracelet pawned in Johor
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Five suspects, including a foreign woman, have been remanded for three days after a bracelet pawned at a pawnshop in Sungai Rengit was found to be fake. District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the three men, a local woman and the foreigner, aged between 34 and 62, were arrested in Sungai Rengit between 1pm and 3pm yesterday. Police did not disclose the amount paid, but a genuine 23-gram 916 gold bracelet could be worth around RM12,000.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines advises extra travel time to KLIA during F1 weekend
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines has advised passengers travelling through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) between Oct 2 and 4 to allow extra time for their journey due to expected traffic congestion during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix Malaysia 2026. Malaysia Airlines also encouraged passengers to consider using the KLIA Ekspres train service to reach the airport. "Malaysia Airlines appreciates passengers' understanding and cooperation during this period," it said.

items.title: SME association welcomes minimum wage increment exemption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's decision to exempt small and medium enterprises (SMEs) from further minimum wage increases will protect 1.3 million SMEs nationwide, said the Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta). Its national president Datuk William Ng welcomed the cabinet decision , which he said would help SMEs cope with rising costs, compressed margins and global economic uncertainties. He said the move demonstrated the government's responsiveness to the challenges faced by SMEs while ensuring workers' welfare remained protected.

items.title: RON97, RON95 prices down 5 sen, diesel 15 sen from Oct 1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Retail prices of unsubsidised RON97 and RON95 petrol will fall by 5 sen per litre, while unsubsidised diesel will drop by 15 sen per litre from Oct 1 to 7. The Finance Ministry (MoF) said the new prices would be RM5 per litre for RON97, RM4.52 per litre for unsubsidised RON95 and RM5.27 per litre for unsubsidised diesel. At the current prices, Budi95 recipients pay RM1.99 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised RON95 price of RM4.52 per litre.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPT 30, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Investor sentiment strengthened on lower oil prices and reduced expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes, lifting the benchmark index. Oil prices extended their recent decline as signs emerged that Middle East crude exports were recovering towards pre-war levels, despite a lack of clear progress in US-Iran talks. Bitcoin slipped to around RM340,776, while Ethereum remained stable at around RM10,961.

items.title: Malaysia, Qatar call for end to West Asia conflicts
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the matter was discussed during a telephone conversation with Qatar's Emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, who called for humanitarian aid to be expedited and peace efforts strengthened to end the suffering of affected communities. Anwar said they discussed the latest developments in peace negotiations and the conflicts in West Asia, particularly the suffering of Palestinians in Gaza and efforts to ease tensions involving Iran. Anwar said Malaysia would continue to support diplomatic efforts with Qatar and regional partners to ensure lasting peace.

items.title: EPF CEO outlines four priorities for Malaysia as Malaysians live longer, says all have role to play
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia now faces four priorities as Malaysians are expected to live longer lives, including shifting from just thinking about having money for retirement to having income for the remaining years, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) CEO said today. EPF CEO Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn noted that longevity is one of the biggest defining forces that will impact Malaysia, including its society and economy. “Income security, health, care, work, and community all shape how well people live longer lives,” the retirement savings fund’s CEO said in his closing remarks at the two-day ISWC 2026 here.

items.title: Fahmi asks MCMC to clarify Meta’s response on WhatsApp issues
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has asked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to issue a statement clarifying Meta’s response to issues involving hacked and deactivated WhatsApp accounts. However, he said he had yet to receive an update on discussions between MCMC and Meta on the matter. Meta had requested until 3 pm last Monday to submit its response to issues raised by MCMC concerning hacked and deactivated WhatsApp accounts.

items.title: Selangor allocates RM100,000 to help wives and children wronged in maintenance issues
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 30 — The Selangor state government has allocated RM100,000 for the implementation of the Selangor Rahmah Maintainence Assistance Programme 2026 to strengthen social protection and welfare for women and children who have been wronged due to syariah judgement debtors. Selangor Women’s Development and Community Welfare Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said that the temporary financial assistance is estimated to benefit up to 50 affected families while the law enforcement process is carried out. He said the one-off assistance was distributed according to the rates set by the Family Support Division (BSK) of the Selangor Syariah Judiciary Department (JAKESS) at RM2,000 for the wife and RM1,000 for each child.

items.title: Johan Setia reports highest unhealthy API level at 166, twenty areas in total experiencing bad air
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Twenty areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4.30 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest level at 166. According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, four other areas in Selangor also recorded unhealthy air quality: Shah Alam (164), Klang (158), Petaling Jaya (155) and Banting (143). Meanwhile, 45 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three were at a good level.

items.title: Sarawak hydrogen market viability still unproven, says analyst
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 30 — Putrajaya should think twice about extending incentives to Sarawak’s hydrogen sector when it has yet to prove that there are enough buyers willing to pay commercially viable prices, according to an analyst. He said the basic problem with hydrogen was not Sarawak’s ability to produce it, but whether anyone wanted to buy enough of it at a price that made the business sustainable. “You can build the plant and produce the hydrogen.

items.title: Flying this weekend? Malaysia Airlines urges KLIA passengers to arrive early amid Sepang F1 traffic
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Malaysia Airlines advises passengers travelling from KL International Airport (KLIA) on Oct 2-4, 2026 to allow additional travel time to the airport, due to expected traffic congestion during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit. “Passengers are advised to arrive at KLIA at least three hours before the scheduled departure time for international flights and two hours before the scheduled departure time for domestic flights to ensure a smooth process. “Malaysia Airlines said the check-in counters close 60 minutes before the scheduled departure time for both domestic and international flights,” it said in a post on X.

items.title: Immigration Dept denies social media claim that Myanmar teen was repatriated, says she remains in detention
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Immigration Department today denied claims that a Myanmar teenage girl was among those repatriated to Myanmar yesterday, saying she remains in custody at an immigration detention depot. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said checks by the department found that the teenager was not involved in the September 29 repatriation programme, which saw Myanmar nationals transported home aboard Myanmar naval vessels. “Checks by the department confirmed that the individual remains detained at an Immigration depot and was not involved in the repatriation programme for Myanmar nationals via Myanmar military vessels yesterday,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Myanmar man gets 16 years’ prison for killing 80-year-old fruit seller in Taman OUG
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — A Myanmar man was sentenced to 16 years’ imprisonment by the High Court today after pleading guilty to causing the death of an elderly fruit seller at a house in Taman OUG, three years ago. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin handed down the sentence on Shofi Husson Fozo Rahman, 29, and ordered the accused to serve the prison term from the date of his arrest on Sept 26, 2023. “The accused behaved well while in prison.

items.title: Primary Six pupil suffers burns after setting off firecrackers, Muar cops probe social media influence
items.summary: The incident also triggered panic among parents and the school community. Muar police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the 12-year-old boy was injured in the incident, which occurred at about 11am. Raiz Mukhliz said initial investigations later led police to detain the pupil to assist in the probe.

items.title: Selangor mulls appeal after High Court finds authorities liable for 2021 Taman Sri Muda floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Selangor government is considering whether to appeal a High Court ruling that found the federal government and two state authorities liable for negligence over the devastating 2021 Taman Sri Muda floods. The High Court yesterday ruled in favour of 50 Taman Sri Muda residents who sued the government and several public authorities over losses they suffered during the catastrophic floods in December 2021. Judicial Commissioner Shoba Rajah Dorai Rajah found the federal government, the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and Shah Alam City Council (MBSA), among the defendants, liable for negligence and related failures that contributed to the residents’ losses.

items.title: DOE: Over 500 hotspots in Kalimantan and Sumatra behind haze in Malaysia
items.summary: Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) reported 327 hotspots in Kalimantan and another 191 in Sumatra yesterday, while one hotspot was detected in Sarawak. “ASMC also reported moderate transboundary haze affecting several areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore and northwestern Borneo,” she said in a statement today. Azuri Azizah said the DOE would continue monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, hotspots and transboundary haze developments, taking meteorological information into account when assessing the situation and coordinating haze management measures at district, state and national levels.

items.title: ‘Dinner, but no deal yet’: Fahmi says nothing formal between Pakatan and Bersatu for now
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — Pakatan Harapan has yet to begin formal discussions with Bersatu over possible cooperation for the Melaka state election, despite a closed-door meeting between representatives of both sides earlier this week. PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said any decision on political cooperation would have to be made by the coalition's presidential council, adding that he had not received any information on formal negotiations with Bersatu. His comments came after PH and Bersatu leaders attended a closed-door dinner in Melaka on Monday night, fuelling speculation that the two sides could be exploring an electoral arrangement ahead of the state election.

items.title: Fahmi: Govt expects F1, KL Marathon and Le Tour de Langkawi to go ahead despite haze
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — The government expects the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Le Tour de Langkawi and Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon to proceed this weekend despite haze affecting several parts of the country, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. “For now, the government expects the three major events — LTdL, F1 and the Standard Chartered Marathon — to continue,” he said during a press conference here. He said Malaysia had also offered assets to Indonesia to help the country tackle fires contributing to the regional haze.

items.title: Touch ‘n Go to add 10 Enhanced RFID lanes for Malaysia’s MLFF transition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Touch ‘n Go Sdn Bhd (Touch ‘n Go) is expanding its Enhanced Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) network with 10 additional lanes by the end of the year to support the country’s transition towards a Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) tolling ecosystem. Currently, two Enhanced RFID lanes are already operational, located at the Ampang-bound Dato Keramat toll plaza on AKLEH, and the Putrajaya-bound Putrajaya toll plaza on the MEX Highway. Woon said the RFID lanes feature an enhanced technology that utilises two RFID antennas paired with an Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) camera.

items.title: KTM Komuter, ETS services resume after Batang Benar-Labu power line repairs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — KTM Komuter Klang Valley and ETS services have resumed normal operations after repair works on the overhead power line between Batang Benar and Labu were completed at 1.41pm today, Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) said. In a statement, KTMB said KTM Komuter and ETS services on the Pulau Sebang-Batu Caves-Pulau Sebang route were operating as usual, although some ETS journeys could still face temporary delays as train movements and schedules are readjusted. Earlier today, Malay Mail reported that services were disrupted from 6.24am after a 25kV overhead power line between Batang Benar and Labu was severed.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia needs young talent to navigate diverse challenges
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — The country needs a younger generation with determination, understanding and knowledge to take on the important responsibilities of driving national development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said young people with such talent and leadership qualities were essential in navigating the various challenges and complexities of the country’s governance. Also present were Deputy Prime Ministers Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, and Cabinet ministers.

items.title: In Johor Bahru, man’s reversing mishap sends car into two vehicles and an eatery
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 30 — A 69-year-old man accidentally crashed his Toyota Camry into two vehicles and an eatery after apparently pressing the accelerator by mistake while reversing in Taman Daya here yesterday. Johor Bahru South police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffie said police were alerted to the incident after videos of it went viral on social media at about 2.20pm. The aftermath of an accident at an eatery in Taman Daya, Johor Bahru, after a Toyota Camry crashed into two vehicles before ploughing into the premises on September 29, 2026.

items.title: Kuala Pilah school death: Five students allege bullying by 16-year-old suspect
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 30 — Five students have come forward to police claiming they had been bullied by the first suspect detained over the death of a Form Two male student in Kuala Pilah last Friday. The media reported that police had detained another 16-year-old male student yesterday in the investigation into the death of a Form Two student in Kuala Pilah last Friday. On Sept 25, a Form Two student was injured in an incident at a school in Kuala Pilah.

items.title: Free Rapid KL shuttle buses to Sepang circuit to run every 10–15 minutes from Oct 2–4
items.summary: According to travel information released by Rapid KL, passengers can board the direct service at KLIA 2, Bandar Baru Enstek and Mitsui Outlet Park. At KLIA 2, passengers can board at the Level 1 bus hub at Bays B1, B2 and B3. From KLIA 2, passengers can board the free Rapid KL shuttle to the Sepang International Circuit.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls for MACC action on Zahid over RM2.1b ministry overspending, cites UiTM precedent
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to initiate an investigation into Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi over an alleged RM2.1 billion budget overrun at the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW). Citing official Finance Ministry figures, Lim noted that KKDW spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved budget of RM1.1 billion. In 2024, the ministry expended RM2 billion against a RM1.3 billion allocation, followed by RM2.3 billion spent against an approved RM1.6 billion in 2025.

items.title: No deal with Pakatan: Azmin says Bersatu preparing to contest Melaka polls alone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia has ruled out working with Pakatan Harapan (PH) or any other political party in the Melaka state election, with secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali saying the party is preparing to contest on its own. Azmin also said Bersatu intended to contest under its own logo, as it did in the Negeri Sembilan state election, Berita Harian reported today. Among those present were Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz, Melaka Bersatu election director Datuk Seri Mohamad Ali Mohamad, Bersatu associate wing chief Datuk Seri R Sanjeevan and Melaka Bersatu information chief Datuk Seri Hishamiddin Abdul Karim.

items.title: Honda Civic driver gets attempted murder charge for ramming policeman at Ipoh roadblock
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 30 — A car wash worker pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of attempting to murder a traffic policeman on Sept 24. K. Viknes, 29, entered the plea after the charge was read out before Judge Norhayati Mohamad Yunus. According to the charge sheet, Viknes, who was driving a Honda Civic, attempted to murder Lance Corporal Badrul Izwany Pauzi, 29, by ramming the vehicle into the victim, knowing that the act could result in death.

items.title: Tanjung Rambutan care centre resident charged with murdering fellow patient
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 30 — A man was charged in the Magistrates’ Court here today with murdering a resident of a care centre in Tanjung Rambutan, near here, on Sept 3. The court, however, recorded no plea from Soo Kim Keong, 51, who is also a resident of the care centre, after the charge was read out before Magistrate Norizan Riduan, as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court. Kim Keong is accused of murdering Chong Mun Long, 28, at the Grace Home Care Centre, Jalan Chemor, Tanjung Rambutan, between 3 am and 4 am on the said day.

items.title: ‘We are always open’: BN still negotiating political cooperation, says Asyraf Wajdi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said talks over Barisan Nasional’s (BN) approach to the Melaka state election are still ongoing, with its political cooperation arrangements yet to be finalised. According to Utusan Malaysia , Asyraf said discussions remained at the leadership level and noted that the Election Commission had yet to announce the election date. Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh had said on Sunday that BN would begin talks with other political groupings ahead of the 16th Melaka state election.

items.title: College student fails to strike out murder charge over Jalan Ampang collision that killed couple
items.summary: High Court Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after allowing the prosecution’s preliminary objection to the application filed by Danish Raman Kamar Kumaresan on August 5. “After examining the submissions of both parties, the court allows the prosecution’s preliminary objection. Accordingly, the accused’s application to strike out the murder charge is dismissed,” said the judge.

items.title: Bidor petrol station shooting: Man hospitalised with bullet wound to shoulder
items.summary: TAPAH, Sept 30 — A 41-year-old man was reportedly shot in the left shoulder after two gunmen opened fire on his four-wheel-drive vehicle at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral yesterday. According to Berita Harian , Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the incident occurred at about 6.08pm after the victim drove his white Toyota Land Cruiser into the station to refuel. Police forensic investigators reportedly recovered one 9mm Luger bullet, four spent cartridge cases of the same calibre and bullet fragments at the scene, while further fragments and bullet marks were found on the victim’s vehicle.

items.title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash: Police find no indication of foul play
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 30 — Police have found no indication of foul play in their investigation into the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash at Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, which claimed five lives, with the probe now nearing completion. Bukit Aman Management director and Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said police had taken statements from several witnesses, including those connected to locations visited by the crew members and the helicopter before the incident. As far as the police investigation is concerned, we have nearly completed our investigation,” he said.
